8:["$","$L13",null,{"data":{"chapterId":23,"verseId":8,"chapterTitle":"Examination of Error","totalVerses":25,"verseData":{"id":"v23_8","number":8,"title":"Form, Sound, Taste, Touch, Smell, and Dharmas Are Like a City of Gandharvas","sanskrit":{"text":"","transliteration":"","translation":"Form, sound, taste, touch, smell, and dharmas are merely like a city of gandharvas, like a mirage, like a dream."},"philosophy":{"insight":"The sense objects (v.7) are characterized as ILLUSORY — like a mirage, a dream, a phantom city. This doesn't mean they don't appear (mirages DO appear) but that they lack inherent reality. Their mode of existence is conventional, not inherent.","madhyamaka":"Rūpa śabda etc. gandharva-nagara-upama svapna-upama marīci-upama (like phantom city, dream, mirage). These are classic Madhyamaka analogies for conventional existence: appearing without inherent reality.","quantum":"Virtual particles: they appear, have measurable effects (Casimir effect), yet aren't \"really there\" permanently. Conventionally effective without being inherently real — like mirages.","bridge":"Both: phenomena that are conventionally effective without being inherently real. QM: virtual particles. V.8: sense objects. Both: effective appearance ≠ inherent reality.","accessible":"A dream apple can make dream-you happy — it's effective within the dream. But it's not a \"real\" apple. Sense objects are like that: effective (they trigger experiences) without being inherently real.","twoTruths":"Conventionally: sense objects appear and function (we see, hear, taste, etc.). Ultimately: they're like mirages — appearing without inherent reality. Convention = dream-reality, not inherent reality.","commonMisconception":"NOT saying the world is an illusion (non-existent). Dreams DO appear. Mirages DO appear. V.8: sense objects DO appear and function. Their MODE of existence is dream-like, not their non-existence."},"quantumResonance":{"concept":"Virtual Particles — Effective Without Permanent Reality","score":55,"strength":"Medium","explanation":"Virtual particles: measurably effective (Casimir effect) yet not permanently real. Dream-like mode of existence."},"deeperDive":[{"q":"What is a \"city of gandharvas\"?","a":"A phantom/mirage city — seen in the distance but with no real foundation. Classic Indian analogy for appearances without inherent existence. The city appears but can't be entered or lived in.","realLifeExample":"A \"puddle\" on a hot road that disappears as you approach — a mirage. It appears but has no substance. Sense objects are like that."},{"q":"Does this mean the world is a dream?","a":"Not that it's non-existent like a square circle. Empty basis → empty dependent (again)."},{"q":"How do virtual particles illustrate this?","a":"Virtual particles appear in quantum calculations, have measurable effects (like the Casimir effect), yet aren't \"really there\" as permanent particles. Enjoy without grasping."},{"q":"Significance for afflictions?","a":"If the sense objects that trigger afflictions are mirage-like, the afflictions they trigger are also mirage-like.
